rows.grounds: demonstrative pronoun referring to the determination

items.question: What restrictive nature defines the determination that nothing else is to be done?
premises: A determination asserts that nothing other is to be done.
Such a determination fixes the scope of possible action.
This fixing takes the form of restraint.
items.inference: The determination limiting action to what must be done is inherently a form of restraint.
uncertainties: The precise referent of the determination depends on the preceding doctrinal context.
items.plain_english: The determination that nothing else is to be done has the nature of restraint.
